sections.h2: Where is Baldwin County, Georgia, and why does its history matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Baldwin County is in central Georgia and its county seat is Milledgeville, which grew along the Oconee River. The Georgia General Assembly created the county on May 11, 1803, and Milledgeville served as the state capital from 1804 to 1868, according to Wikipedia.

That history shows up in the housing stock. The historic district, the Old Capitol building (now home to Georgia Military College) and the campus of Georgia College and State University mean Milledgeville has a wide mix of old and new houses, across a range of ages and sizes. The General Assembly provided for Central State Hospital in 1837, another long-running institution tied to the city.

The county covers 267 square miles and lies on the fall line, with hillier Piedmont terrain to the north and flatter coastal plain to the south. The part of the county south of Lake Sinclair drains to the Lower Oconee River basin. Putnam, Hancock, Washington, Wilkinson and Jones counties surround it. Besides Milledgeville, the only other named places are the Hardwick census-designated place and the unincorporated community of Scottsboro.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about the Baldwin County housing market?
sections.html:
Baldwin County has a noticeably lower owner-occupancy rate than most rural Georgia counties in this group. The Census Bureau lists 61.1 percent of housing units as owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024, and a median value of $181,900.

The 2020 census recorded 19,988 housing units, with 17.4 percent vacant and 42.1 percent of occupied units rented. Population slipped 4.2 percent between 2010 and 2020, then edged up about half a percent in the Census estimates through 2025.

About 31.7 percent of the county's 16,511 households were people living alone in 2020, and the median age was 38.4. The 2020 count put 51.2 percent of residents in urban areas and 48.8 percent in rural areas, so a Baldwin County seller might own a city lot in Milledgeville or a rural parcel out in the county.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Baldwin County?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's office is at the Baldwin County Government Building, 1601 N. Columbia Street, Suite 100, Milledgeville, GA 31061. The Baldwin County tax site lists 478-445-4813 and hours of 8:30 am to 4:45 pm Monday through Friday, closed on holidays.

Valuation questions go to the tax assessors at (478) 445-5300, and parcel data is on qPublic. A five-member Board of Commissioners, elected from single-member districts, sets the county side of the millage rate, and the Board of Education sets the school side.

  • Tax commissioner: billing, payment, liens and closing statements
  • Tax assessors: values, returns, exemptions and appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens

sections.h2: When is the Baldwin County tax bill due, and what does late payment cost?
sections.html:
Read the date printed on your bill, because the county's own pages give two. The General Information page says Baldwin County property taxes are due by December 15, while the Tax Bill Information page says they are generally due by November 15, with bills mailed at least 60 days earlier.

Payment can be split into two installments, and any unpaid balance keeps accruing charges. A mailed check must be postmarked by the due date. If the date falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies. A drop box is in the front lot, and card payments carry a processor fee of 2.57 percent (3 percent for American Express) with a $1.50 minimum.

  • Interest: bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, accruing monthly after the due date
  • Penalty: 5 percent of the tax due at 120 days past the due date, repeating every 120 days up to 20 percent
  • The penalty skips homesteaded property with a bill under $500
  • Mobile homes: tax due April 1, with a 10 percent penalty and possible citation if unpaid

sections.h2: How do I sell a Baldwin County house when the tax bill is still open?
sections.html:
Ask the tax commissioner for a payoff figure and let the closing agent pay it from your proceeds. Georgia puts the whole year's tax on the January 1 owner, and Baldwin County's office says a lien is recorded in that owner's name unless it receives a closing statement showing the buyer took responsibility within 90 days of the due date.

If you sold during the year and a bill still arrives in your name, forward it to the buyer and send the office a copy of the settlement statement. Unpaid tax leads to a recorded lien on the General Execution Docket in the Clerk's office, and the county says that lien can remain on a credit record for at least seven years.

If the house was a rental, an estate property or has been vacant, request the full tax history for every year you owned it before you set a closing date, so no earlier year surprises you at the table.

sections.h2: How does a Baldwin County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the assessment notice to appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. Grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and the state supplies a uniform form.

The same filing must name your route. A Board of Equalization hearing is the standard path, and the assessors may first revise the value and send a new notice you can appeal within 30 days. A hearing officer, who must be a certified appraiser, is available for non-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or more, according to the Baldwin tax site. Arbitration needs a certified appraisal, and its result cannot be appealed further. After the Board of Equalization or hearing officer, Superior Court is the next step.

Georgia's Department of Revenue notes that it cannot override the local assessors, the board, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or the court on an individual valuation.

sections.h2: What exemptions apply in Baldwin County?
sections.html:
The county offers local homestead exemptions in addition to the state's, and the larger one governs. File with the assessors; the application must be received by April 1 of the first year you claim, and it renews automatically afterward.

  • Owner-occupied on January 1 of the first year
  • No homestead claimed on any other property in Georgia or another state
  • Property tax deferral for homeowners 62 or older with household income of $15,000 or less
  • Agricultural assessment at 30 percent, plus conservation use and forest land programs with 10 or 15 year covenants

Call (478) 445-5300 for the current local amounts, and bring proof of age, income or service if you claim an exemption that depends on them.

sections.h2: Where do Baldwin County deeds and liens get recorded?
sections.html:
The Clerk of Superior Court keeps the deed records and the General Execution Docket, which is where an unpaid tax lien is recorded. A tax lien that has not been paid will show up when a title company searches the parcel, so a seller who pays the balance before listing avoids a delay.

The tax commissioner's site adds that the office does not send delinquent notices every month, only at intervals, and tells owners to verify the amount due before paying. For a Baldwin County sale, ask for the payoff in writing with the date it was calculated, since interest accrues monthly and a figure from last week may be short.

Closing agents in Milledgeville routinely collect the tax payoff from the seller's proceeds. Give yours the tax commissioner's phone number, 478-445-4813, early in the process.

faqs.q: Which Baldwin County office do I call about my tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the tax commissioner at 478-445-4813. The office is at 1601 N. Columbia Street, Suite 100, Milledgeville, and is open weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:45 pm.

faqs.q: Can I pay Baldwin County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, the county runs an online payment page, and card payments carry the processor fee described on the tax site. You can also pay by mail, at the counter or in the drop box.

faqs.q: Will selling in Baldwin County cancel my tax bill?
faqs.a: No. A sale does not erase the bill for the year. The January 1 owner stays on the record unless the office receives the closing statement within 90 days of the due date, so send it promptly.

faqs.q: What is the assessed percentage in Baldwin County?
faqs.a: Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value under Georgia law, and agricultural land that qualifies can be assessed at 30 percent. Exemptions are subtracted before the millage rate applies.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Baldwin County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date of the assessment notice. Mobile home owners have 45 days from the mailing of the tax bill or April 1, whichever is later.
